verdict.rationale: Groq's docs position it as fast LLM inference with service tiers tunable for latency and throughput, a Flex tier optimized for high-throughput workloads, and streaming of completion deltas. Independent hands-on reports corroborate very high generation speed (450–491 tokens/sec on Mixtral), and Groq staff describe low latency with no queuing even at batch size 1. Missing for 10: quantified time-to-first-token measurements, and first-party published latency/throughput figures (current speed evidence comes from older community tests).

support.subject: As a developer, I can serve latency-sensitive workloads with fast time-to-first-token and high-throughput generation

citations.quote: Groq offers multiple service tiers so you can tune for latency, throughput, and reliability.
Flex Processing is a service tier optimized for high-throughput workloads that prioritizes fast inference
you can stream the model's response in real-time. This allows your application to display the response as it's being generated
I'm achieving consistent 450+ tokens/sec for Mixtral 8x7b 32k and ~200 tps for Llama 2 70B-4k.
our LPU architecture allows us to deliver good throughput even at batch size 1.
our system is deterministic, no need for waiting or queuing anywhere, and we can have very low latency interconnect between cards.
